newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Youths riot in French Guiana, set building ablaze.
newsitem.headline: Youths riot in French Guiana, set building ablaze.

text.p: Rioting youths hurled firebombs at a government building, set fire to cars and looted shops in a night of rioting in Cayenne, capital of French Guiana.

Pierre Dartout, the administrator in the French overseas department on the northeastern coast of South America, described the incidents on Thursday night and early on Friday as premeditated and "very serious".
"Cars were destroyed, stores looted and public buildings attacked, some being seriously damaged," he told the local state-owned radio.
"The intervention by civilian and military police was made necessary to assure the security of the prefecture and the persons - civil servants and students who were there," he added.

"When police charged rocks and bottles were thrown inside the prefecture causing damage to the building and injuring persons. Well organised groups having prepared Molotov cocktails beforehand started violent incidents...The groups behind this riot had prepared their action well in advance with the aim of destabilisation," Dartout said.

He personnally had been barricaded for several hours inside the Cayenne prefecture by high school students who burned tyres and threw rocks in protest against poor conditions in local schools, witnesses said.
Extensive damage also resulted from a fire at French Guiana's Regional Council headquarters several blocks from the prefecture after youths hurled firebombs at the building.
Regional Council president Antoine Karam said the damage amounted to at least 10 million French francs ($2 million).
State-owned radio said one youth was injured by rifle fire by a local resident and unconfirmed reports said five other peoples were injured, four of them riot police.
French Guiana's economy lags behind mainland France and it has an unemployment rate approaching 25 percent of the labour force. Joblessness is particularly prevalent among the young.
Dozens of riot police surrounded the Cayenne prefecture building in anticipation of new violence, witnesses said.
